_about.what: Gym — upper body & conditioning — one move per object in "moves". The app reads this file directly: save it, reload the page. Every field name is checked, so a typo is reported with the file and move it is in.
_about.add: Copy a move that looks like the new one, paste it into "moves", give it a new id and change every field. Or: node scripts/catalog.js new <file> <id>  — writes a template with placeholder text to replace.
_about.remove: Delete the move's object (and the comma before or after it). Routines built in the app that used it will show it as missing.
_about.check: node scripts/catalog.js check  — or reload the app: a bad file shows the error on screen instead of the exercise list.
_about.names: Anything written as a word instead of an object — "metric": "knee", "template": "lean", "preset": "standing", "conditions": "balance" — is looked up in shared.json. Add reusable pieces there, not here.
_about.notes: Any field starting with "_" is a note for people and is ignored: "_note": "physio wants this re-checked".

fields.id: Unique name, used in links and saved sessions — never change it once the move has been used. Lower-case letters, digits, underscores. Good: "seated_knee_ext". Bad: "Seated Knee Ext", "knee-ext", "1_knee".
fields.name: What the user sees in the list. Good: "Seated knee extension". Bad: a clinical term nobody outside physio uses ("Open-chain terminal extension").
fields.clinicalName: Optional. The term a physio would use, shown in the details panel under the name.
fields.type: "reps" (counted) or "hold" (seconds in position). A stretch held for 30 s is a hold; ten slow raises are reps.
fields.view: "side" or "front" — where the phone stands. Side-on for anything that bends forward/back (knees, hips, spine); front-on for anything that goes out to the side (leg raise to the side, arm raise to the side, knees caving in).
fields.tracking: What the camera can honestly do: "form" (counts AND judges — needs at least one fault with a measurement and a threshold), "reps" (counts only; faults are listed for the person to watch), "none" (nothing to measure — the guide is shown and the set is logged by hand). Bad: "form" on a move whose faults are all words; the file will not load.
fields.vetted: Optional, true/false. true = a physio has recorded and checked this move in the Studio; vetted moves list first.
fields.equipment: List of words: ["none"], ["chair"], ["band", "door anchor"]. Optional extras say so: "ankle weight (optional)".
fields.muscles: { "primary": [...], "secondary": [...] } — plain names ("quadriceps", "gluteus medius"). primary must have at least one.
fields.sided: Only for one-sided moves: { "limb": "leg" | "arm" | "side", "by": "camera" | "pick", "auto": true }. "camera" = the limb nearest the phone is the working one (side-on moves); "pick" = the person chooses (front-on moves); "auto": true = when no side was chosen, watch both and follow the one that moves. Leave the field out for two-sided moves.
fields.upperBody: true when the legs need not be in frame (seated desk moves, shoulder work). Default false.
fields.summary: One line for the list. Good: "Sitting, straighten one knee until the leg is level, hold, and lower." Bad: a paragraph.
fields.setup: Where the phone goes and how to start, in the user's words. Good: "Sit tall on a chair, side-on to the phone, working leg nearest…" Bad: "Standard set-up."
fields.why: Why this camera angle can measure this move. Shown to the user; keeps the author honest. Good: "Side-on the knee angle runs from 90° to straight." Bad: left empty.
fields.calibrationPose: Optional. The still position held for the first two seconds of every set, which the coach measures against. Good: "Sitting tall, knee bent to 90°, foot hanging."
fields.camera: { "height": "floor" | "knee" | "hip" | "chest" | "eye", "distance": "2 m", "posture": "standing" | "sitting" | "lying" | "prone" | "sidelying" | "kneeling" }. Leave it out to use the file's default at the top. posture also decides how the stick figure is pinned in place.
fields.targets: Optional list of rep counts / hold seconds the bubble cycles through, e.g. [6, 8, 10, 12]. Leave it out for the standard choices in settings.json.
fields.defaultTarget: The one of targets selected to begin with. Must be in the list. Leave it out with targets.
fields.progress: How far through a rep the person is. { "metric": <measurement>, "start": "calibrated" | number, "target": number | "opt:rom" }. "calibrated" = whatever the measurement reads in the start position; "startMin"/"startMax" clamp it (a knee that calibrates at 150° is treated as 160°). target = the reading at a full rep, or with "targetIsDelta": true a change from the start — "delta": -1 when the reading goes DOWN during the rep (a knee angle closing). Only for type "reps" with tracking "form" or "reps". Good: knee angle from calibrated to 172. Bad: start and target the same number.
fields.hold: For type "hold" with tracking on: { "conditions": [ { "metric": <measurement>, "rel": "abs" | "change", "min": n, "max": n } ] } — the hold counts while every condition is met. "change" = relative to the calibrated start. A condition may carry "when": [{ "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }] so it only applies for that option. A named set ("balance") comes from shared.json.
fields.display: Optional. What the live readout shows: { "label": "bend", "unit": "°", "from": "start" } shows the progress measurement as a change from the start ("abs" = the raw reading); for a hold, { "condition": 0, "label": "knee", "aim": "90°" } shows that hold condition. Without it the app shows the raw progress reading.
fields.enterCue: Optional, holds only: what the coach says when the person has been out of position for a few seconds. Good: "Slide down the wall until your knees are at ninety".
fields.faults: What goes wrong, in the order they matter. Each: { "id", "label", "cue" (spoken, ≤ 8 words, what TO do), "tip" (written, why it matters), "severity" 1–3 }. Add "metric", "op" ("<" or ">"), "threshold" and the camera watches for it; leave those out and it is listed for the person to watch. "minP" (0–1) = ignore until this far into the rep; "persist" ms before it is spoken; "rel": "change" compares to the calibrated start. "when": a list of gates that must all hold for the fault to count — { "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }, { "metric": <measurement>, "op": "<", "threshold": 168 }, "inPosition" or "notInPosition". "phase": "moving" / "rest" (reps) or "any" (a hold fault that must fire while the person is OUT of position; otherwise hold faults only watch the held position). "scale": { "metric": "progress", "times": 0.35 } makes the threshold grow with another reading. Rules instead of a measurement: "rule": "shallow" (rep did not reach the target), "fast" with "minMs", "return" with "threshold" (rep ended above this progress — did not come all the way back). Or "template": "lean" with a "threshold" to reuse one from shared.json. Good cue: "Sit tall". Bad cue: "You are leaning back again" (tells them what is wrong, not what to do).
fields.guide: { "surface": what to stand/lie on, "stop": when to stop, "cannotSee": what the person must check themselves, "regions": [ { "name": "Trunk", "points": [ { "t": "one form point", "tracked": true|false } ] } ] }. tracked: true only when a fault with a measurement actually checks that point — it is shown to the user as "camera watches".
fields.pose: The two-frame stick figure. { "A": start keyframe, "B": end keyframe, "work": { "thigh": 1, "glute": 0.5 } muscles to light up 0–1, "props": [ { "kind": "box" | "bar" | "disc" | "band", "at": "hip" } ], "wall": "behind" | "ahead", "anchor": joint(s) that stay put }. Side-view keyframe angles in degrees: torso (from vertical, + = leaning forward), thigh & shin (from hanging straight down, + = forward), foot (+ = toes up), uarm & farm (arms, + = forward), plus the far limb: thighF, shinF, footF, uarmF, farmF; face: "right" | "left". Front-view: legL, legR, shinL, shinR, armL, armR, foreL, foreR (+ = out to the side), lean, headTilt, squat 0–1. "preset": "standing" | "seated" | "supine" | "prone" | "quadruped" fills the usual values first. Check it on /figures.html.
fields.tempo: Free text. Good: "Up 2 s, hold 2 s, down 3 s."
fields.contraindications: When not to do it. Shown as "Do not do this if".
fields.sources: Optional list of { "name", "url" } added to the file's own sources.
fields.band: Optional. "none", "yellow", "red"… = offers the band-colour bubble with that default; true = offers it defaulting to none.
fields.minMs: Optional, reps only: the quickest a rep may take before "Too fast" fires (when the move lists no live fault of its own). Default in settings.json.
fields.options: Advanced: extra bubbles, e.g. a range target { "key": "rom", "label": "Range target", "values": [45, 60, 75, 90], "unit": "°", "default": 90 } referenced from progress.target as "opt:rom".
fields.figure: Advanced: point keyframes captured by the Studio instead of pose angles. Prefer pose.
fields.focus: Advanced: the landmark the live view highlights, e.g. "KNEE". Default: the last point of the progress measurement.
fields.group: Optional. The heading the move is listed under; default = the file's group at the top.
fields.region: Optional. The body region for filtering; default = the file's region.
fields.icon: Optional short label used where an icon is expected. Default "move".
fields.order: Optional. Position in the list; default = the file's order + position in this file.

moves.name: Push-up
moves.summary: Hands under the shoulders, body straight, lower the chest to a fist from the floor and press up.
moves.setup: Side-on to the phone at floor level, hands just wider than the shoulders, toes on the floor, body one line. Lower until the chest is a fist-height from the floor, elbows about 45° from the body, and press back up.
moves.why: From the side the elbow angle gives depth and the hips should sit on the line from shoulder to ankle; sagging or piking off it is measured directly.
moves.contraindications: Wrist or shoulder pain in the bottom position.

faults.label: Hips sagging
faults.tip: Squeeze the glutes and brace so the body stays one line.

faults.label: Hips piking up
faults.tip: A tent shape shortens the movement; lower the hips to the line.

faults.label: Elbows flaring wide
faults.tip: Arrow, not T: elbows halfway between tucked and wide.

guide.surface: Firm floor; a mat under the hands is fine.
guide.cannotSee: The elbow flare — a top-down detail.

points.t: Straight from shoulder to ankle throughout.
Chest a fist from the floor.

moves.name: Incline push-up
moves.summary: Hands on a raised surface, body straight, lower the chest to it and press away.
moves.setup: Hands on a bench or table edge, side-on to the phone, body one line from head to heels. Lower the chest toward the edge and press back up.
moves.why: From the side the elbow angle closes and opens each rep, so reps are counted. The body line is listed, not judged, because the bench often hides the hip.
moves.progression: Lower surface, down to the floor.

faults.label: Hips sagging
faults.tip: Brace so the body stays one line.

faults.label: Cutting depth
faults.tip: Touch the chest to the surface each rep.

guide.cannotSee: The hips when the bench is in the way.

moves.name: Knee push-up
moves.summary: From the knees, body straight from head to knee, lower the chest to the floor and press up.
moves.setup: Kneel side-on to the phone at floor level, hands under the shoulders, hips forward so the body is one line from shoulder to knee. Lower the chest toward the floor and press up.
moves.why: From the side the elbow angle closes and opens each rep, so reps are counted.

faults.label: Hips bending
faults.tip: Push the hips forward so the line from shoulder to knee is straight; do not sit back.

faults.label: Cutting depth
faults.tip: Lower until the chest nearly touches.

moves.name: Pike push-up
moves.summary: Hips high in an inverted V, lower the head toward the floor between the hands and press up.
moves.setup: Hands and feet on the floor, hips pushed high so the body makes an upside-down V, side-on to the phone at floor level. Bend the elbows to lower the top of the head toward the floor, then press back up.
moves.why: From the side the elbow angle closes each rep, so reps are counted.
moves.contraindications: Shoulder or wrist pain; high blood pressure when the head is low.

faults.label: Hips dropping
faults.tip: Keep the hips stacked over the shoulders so the press is vertical.

faults.label: Cutting depth
faults.tip: Lower until the head nearly touches.

guide.stop: Shoulder or wrist pain, or dizziness.

points.t: Bend to lower the head; press to straight.

moves.name: Bench dip
moves.summary: Hands on a bench behind you, lower the hips by bending the elbows and press back up.
moves.setup: Sit on the edge of a bench, hands beside the hips, then walk the feet out and lift off, side-on to the phone. Lower the hips by bending the elbows to about 90°, keeping the back close to the bench, then press up.
moves.why: From the side the elbow angle closes each rep, so reps are counted.
moves.progression: Feet on a second bench; weight on the lap.
moves.contraindications: Front-of-shoulder pain — this move is hard on irritable shoulders.

faults.label: Going too deep
faults.tip: Below 90° the front of the shoulder takes the strain.

faults.label: Hips drifting forward
faults.tip: Keep the back brushing the bench so the triceps do the work.

points.t: Bend to a right angle; point straight back.

moves.name: Pull-up
moves.summary: Hang from a bar with palms away, pull until the chin passes it, lower to straight arms.
moves.setup: Hang from the bar, hands just wider than the shoulders, palms away, facing the phone. Pull the elbows down to bring the chin over the bar, then lower fully.
moves.why: Facing the phone the elbow angle closes and opens each rep, so reps are counted. Kipping and the chin actually clearing the bar are not judged.

faults.label: Swinging or kicking
faults.tip: Legs quiet, no swing; if you need momentum, use a band.

faults.label: Not lowering fully
faults.tip: Each rep starts from a full hang.

guide.surface: A bar rated for body weight.

points.t: Straight at the bottom; elbows drive down to the ribs.

moves.name: Chin-up
moves.summary: Hang with palms facing you, shoulder-width, pull the chin over the bar, lower fully.
moves.setup: Hang from the bar, palms facing you, hands shoulder-width, facing the phone. Pull until the chin clears the bar, lower to straight arms.
moves.why: Facing the phone the elbow angle closes and opens each rep, so reps are counted.
moves.contraindications: Elbow or wrist pain with the underhand grip.

faults.label: Swinging
faults.tip: No momentum; use a band if needed.

faults.label: Not lowering fully
faults.tip: Each rep starts from a full hang.

guide.surface: A bar rated for body weight.

points.t: Straight at the bottom; full pull.

moves.name: Inverted row
equipment: low bar, rings or sturdy table
moves.summary: Hanging under a low bar with heels on the floor and body straight, pull the chest to the bar.
moves.setup: Lie under a bar at hip height, grip it, heels on the floor, body straight, side-on to the phone. Pull the chest to the bar with the elbows driving back, then lower under control.
moves.why: From the side the elbow angle closes each rep, so reps are counted. The hips sagging is listed, not judged, because the bar often hides them.

faults.label: Hips sagging
faults.tip: Squeeze the glutes so the body moves as one plank.

faults.label: Not reaching the bar
faults.tip: Pull until the chest touches; if you cannot, raise the bar.

guide.surface: A bar that cannot roll or tip.
guide.cannotSee: The hips when the bar hides them.

points.t: Elbows drive back; chest reaches the bar.

moves.name: Bent-over dumbbell row
moves.summary: Hinged forward with a flat back, row the dumbbells to the hips with the elbows driving back.
moves.setup: Stand side-on to the phone, dumbbells hanging, hinge until the trunk is about 45° with the back flat. Row the weights to the hips, elbows brushing the ribs, then lower under control without standing up.
moves.why: From the side the elbow angle gives each row, and the trunk rising with the weight — the way people cheat — shows as the shoulder–hip line lifting.
moves.tempo: Up 1 s, squeeze 1 s, down 2 s.
moves.regression: One arm with the other hand on a bench.
moves.contraindications: Lower back pain in the hinge.

faults.label: Standing up with the weight
faults.tip: The trunk holds still; if it rises, the weight is too heavy.

faults.label: Back rounding
faults.tip: Brace and keep the chest proud; lower the weight if it rounds.

guide.cannotSee: The back rounding under a shirt.

points.t: Elbows drive back to the hips.

moves.name: One-arm dumbbell row
moves.summary: One hand on a bench, row a dumbbell to the hip with the other, elbow close to the body.
moves.setup: Place one hand and knee on a bench, back flat, dumbbell in the free hand, working arm nearest the phone. Row the weight to the hip with the elbow driving back, then lower fully.
moves.why: From the side the elbow angle closes each rep, so reps are counted. The trunk twisting to help is listed, not judged.
moves.tempo: Up 1 s, squeeze 1 s, down 2 s.

faults.label: Trunk twisting to lift
faults.tip: The chest stays facing the floor; the arm does the work.

faults.label: Not reaching the hip
faults.tip: Finish with the elbow behind the body.

points.t: Elbow drives back past the ribs.

moves.name: Overhead press
moves.summary: Dumbbells at the shoulders, press straight up until the arms lock out overhead, lower.
moves.setup: Face the phone, dumbbells at shoulder height, elbows under the wrists. Press straight up until the arms lock out, then lower to the shoulders.
moves.why: Facing the phone the wrists travel from the shoulders to straight overhead each rep, and the shoulders hiking up to help is measured as the ear–shoulder gap closing.
moves.contraindications: Shoulder pain overhead; lower back pain with the press.

faults.label: Lower back arching
faults.tip: Brace the stomach and squeeze the glutes so the press does not come from leaning back.

faults.label: Not locking out
faults.tip: Finish with the biceps by the ears.

guide.cannotSee: The back arching — a side-view detail.

moves.name: Lateral raise
moves.summary: Light dumbbells by the sides, raise the arms out to shoulder height with soft elbows, lower slowly.
moves.setup: Face the phone, light dumbbells by the sides, slight bend in the elbows. Raise the arms out to the sides until they are level with the shoulders, pause, lower slowly.
moves.why: Facing the phone the wrists rise to shoulder height each rep, the shoulders hiking up shows as the ear–shoulder gap closing, and going above shoulder height is caught too.
moves.regression: Lighter; one arm with the other hand on a support.
moves.contraindications: Shoulder pain lifting to the side (impingement).

faults.label: Raising above the shoulders
faults.tip: Above level the trapezius takes over and the joint pinches.

faults.label: Swinging the weights up
faults.tip: If you need a swing, the weight is too heavy.

guide.stop: A pinch at the top of the shoulder.

points.t: Rise to shoulder height, not above; soft elbows.

moves.name: Front raise
moves.summary: Dumbbells in front of the thighs, raise the straight arms forward to shoulder height, lower slowly.
moves.setup: Stand side-on to the phone, dumbbells in front of the thighs. Raise both arms forward, elbows nearly straight, until level with the shoulders, then lower slowly.
moves.why: From the side the arms swing from hanging to horizontal each rep, so reps are counted.

faults.label: Leaning back
faults.tip: Leaning back cheats the lift; brace and stay upright.

faults.label: Swinging the weights
faults.tip: Lower the weight rather than swing it.

guide.cannotSee: The shoulders shrugging — a front-view detail.

points.t: Rise to shoulder height, nearly straight.

moves.name: Biceps curl
moves.summary: Dumbbell hanging, curl it to the shoulder with the elbow pinned to the side, lower slowly.
moves.setup: Stand side-on to the phone, working arm nearest, dumbbell hanging with the palm forward. Curl to the shoulder without the elbow moving, then lower slowly to straight.
moves.why: From the side the elbow angle gives each curl, and the upper arm swinging forward — the usual cheat — shows as the shoulder–elbow line leaving vertical.
moves.regression: Lighter; seated with the back supported.
moves.contraindications: Elbow or wrist pain under load.

faults.label: Not straightening fully
faults.tip: Each rep starts from a straight arm.

points.t: Pinned to the side; bends fully and straightens fully.

moves.name: Hammer curl
moves.summary: Like a biceps curl but with the palm facing in, thumb up.
moves.setup: Stand side-on to the phone, working arm nearest, dumbbell hanging with the palm facing the thigh. Curl to the shoulder with the elbow still, lower slowly.
moves.why: From the side the elbow angle gives each curl, so reps are counted.

faults.label: Upper arm swinging
faults.tip: Only the forearm moves.

faults.label: Not straightening fully
faults.tip: Start each rep from straight.

points.t: Still by the side; full range.

moves.name: Triceps kickback
moves.summary: Hinged forward with the upper arm held level, straighten the elbow behind you, then bend.
moves.setup: Hinge forward with one hand on a bench, working arm nearest the phone, upper arm level with the back and elbow bent. Straighten the arm fully behind you, squeeze, then bend back to 90°.
moves.why: From the side the elbow angle opens to straight each rep, so reps are counted.
moves.tempo: Out 1 s, squeeze 1 s, back 2 s.

faults.label: Upper arm dropping
faults.tip: The elbow stays high by the ribs; if it drops, the weight is too heavy.

faults.label: Swinging the weight
faults.tip: Straighten under control; no flick.

points.t: Straightens fully; upper arm stays level.

moves.name: Overhead triceps extension
moves.summary: One dumbbell held overhead in both hands, lower it behind the head by bending the elbows, press back up.
moves.setup: Stand side-on to the phone, one dumbbell held overhead with both hands. Keeping the upper arms by the ears, bend the elbows to lower the weight behind the head, then press to straight.
moves.why: From the side the elbow angle closes and opens each rep, so reps are counted.

faults.label: Elbows flaring out
faults.tip: Point the elbows at the ceiling, not out to the sides.

faults.label: Lower back arching
faults.tip: Brace so the weight overhead does not pull the back into an arch.

points.t: Bend fully behind the head; upper arms stay by the ears.

moves.name: Farmer carry
moves.summary: Heavy weights in each hand, walk tall for distance or time.
moves.setup: Pick up a heavy weight in each hand. Stand tall, shoulders back, and walk with short, steady steps for the distance or time.
moves.why: Walking takes you out of frame. Logged by hand.

faults.label: Leaning to one side
faults.tip: Brace the sides of the trunk; the weights should not tip you.

faults.label: Shoulders shrugging
faults.tip: Let the arms hang long from a packed shoulder.

guide.cannotSee: You — the exercise walks out of frame.

moves.name: Mountain climber
moves.summary: From a high plank, drive one knee toward the chest, then switch legs fast.
moves.setup: High plank, hands under the shoulders. Bring one knee toward the chest, return it, then the other, keeping the hips low and steady. Continue for the count.
moves.why: The legs cross under the body too fast and too close together to count reliably. Logged by hand.
moves.contraindications: Wrist or shoulder pain; back pain.

faults.label: Hips rising
faults.tip: Keep the body in a plank line; the knee comes to the chest under it.

faults.label: Bouncing the hips
faults.tip: The legs move; the trunk does not.

guide.cannotSee: The legs — too fast and overlapping.

points.t: Plank line, hips low and still.

moves.name: Burpee
moves.summary: Squat, hands to the floor, jump the feet back to a plank, back in, and jump up.
moves.setup: From standing, squat and put the hands down, jump the feet back to a plank (add a push-up if you like), jump them back in, and jump up with the arms overhead.
moves.why: The body goes from standing to lying to jumping — the calibrated counter cannot follow it. Logged by hand.
moves.dosage: 3 × 10, or as many as possible in a minute.
moves.regression: Step the feet back and in; no jump.
moves.contraindications: Wrist, shoulder, knee or back injury; anyone told to avoid impact.

faults.label: Hips sagging in the plank
faults.cue: Brace before the feet go back
faults.tip: The hips land level with the shoulders, not below.

faults.label: Back rounding on the way up
faults.tip: Land the feet wide enough to stand with the chest up.

guide.cannotSee: The whole thing — the calibrated pose is lost.

moves.name: Plank shoulder tap
moves.summary: From a high plank, lift one hand to tap the opposite shoulder without the hips turning.
moves.setup: High plank facing the phone, feet a little wider than the hips. Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder, replace it, then the other. Keep the hips dead still.
moves.why: The hand crosses the body and the hips twist toward the phone — a top-down detail. Logged by hand.

faults.label: Hips rocking side to side
faults.tip: Widen the feet and brace before each tap; if the hips rock, slow down.

faults.label: Hips sagging
faults.tip: Squeeze the glutes.

points.t: Taps the opposite shoulder and returns.

moves.name: Reverse fly
moves.summary: Hinged forward, raise light dumbbells out to the sides with soft elbows, squeezing the shoulder blades.
moves.setup: Hinge forward until the trunk is near level, dumbbells hanging under the shoulders, soft elbows. Raise the arms out to the sides, squeezing the blades together, then lower slowly.
moves.why: Hinged over, the arms sweep toward and away from a front phone and the trunk hides them from the side. Logged by hand.
moves.tempo: Up 2 s, squeeze 1 s, down 2 s.
moves.regression: Lighter; chest supported on an incline bench.
moves.contraindications: Lower back pain in the hinge.

faults.label: Standing up as the arms lift
faults.tip: The trunk holds still; if it rises, the weight is too heavy.

faults.label: Shrugging
faults.tip: Lead with the elbows out, not up.

points.t: Sweep out to the sides; blades squeeze.

moves.name: Bear crawl
moves.summary: On hands and feet with the knees hovering, crawl forward moving opposite hand and foot together.
moves.setup: Hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips and lifted a few centimetres. Move the right hand and left foot forward together, then the other pair, keeping the back flat and the hips low.
moves.why: Crawling takes you out of frame. Logged by hand.

faults.label: Hips rising
faults.tip: Imagine a plate balanced on the lower back.

faults.label: Hips swaying
faults.tip: Shorter steps keep the hips still.

guide.cannotSee: You — the exercise crawls out of frame.
